gaps.sentence: You cannot enter the studio unless you ___ a visitor badge.
gaps.explanation: Rules with 'unless' keep the present simple: wear.

gaps.sentence: Should you ___ any problems, please contact support.
gaps.explanation: 'Should you plus infinitive' is a formal way to say 'If you ...': experience.

gaps.sentence: I will note the reference number in case I ___ it later.
gaps.hint: in case means as a precaution
gaps.explanation: 'In case' describes a precaution and takes the present simple: need.

gaps.sentence: Unless the strike ___, flights will be grounded all weekend.
gaps.hint: unless plus a present passive verb
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' clauses use the present simple, here in the passive: is called off.

gaps.sentence: I will be surprised if he ___ on time for once.
gaps.explanation: The if-clause of a real future condition takes the present simple: arrives.

gaps.sentence: If you mix blue and yellow, you always ___ green.
gaps.explanation: The adverb 'always' signals a timeless result, so the present simple fits: get.

gaps.sentence: If only we ___ the tickets before they sold out!
gaps.explanation: 'If only' plus the past perfect regrets a missed past opportunity: had bought.

gaps.sentence: As long as you ___ the rules, you will have no problems here.
gaps.hint: as long as states the condition
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' introduces the condition and takes the present simple: follow.
